newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures little changed after refinery news.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures little changed after refinery news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were slightly weaker on Monday as traders and brokers awaited the open of U.S. markets.
September Brent was four cents a barrel weaker at 1139 GMT and stood at $18.91, while August gas oil was 50 cents a tonne firmer at $172.00.
"It is absolutely dead. We are just waiting for the NYMEX open," one dealer at the IPE said.
Gasoline prices jumped in Europe on Friday , pulling the whole energy complex up following news of technical problems with three catalytic crackers in northwest Europe.

But on Monday a cracker at one of these, BP/Texaco's Nerefco's Europoort, was back in operation and a spokesman for a second, BP/Mobil's Coryton refinery, said that would restart within two or three days.
Oil traders anxiously waitied for signs of when Iraqi exports resume under an oil-for-food deal with the U.N. Exports have been delayed by wrangling over an aid distribution plan.
"The crude market is still waiting for news on the Iraqi distribution plan, which is why many participants have been cautious following the latest rally," brokers GNI said in a daily report.
"Once approval is given contractual matters will probably take a few days to complete, so shipments could actually begin next week - that is the most optimistic time frame."
